clarity.justification: The method directly tests the linear-readout hypothesis by computing "cosine(delta, v_T) for the matching trait and all mismatched traits," with directional predictions that the matching direction yields the largest projection and that projection magnitude correlates with behavioral strength. Refuting outcomes are readily decidable—failure of top-1 identification, absent matched-versus-mismatched gaps or correlations, and the failure of the projected "trait-only" delta to express the trait—although no numeric decision thresholds are supplied. The broader assertion that projection predicts expression "better than any surface property" is not fully supported by testing only "n-gram/entropy logistic regression," and the alternative ways of creating teachers "by prompting/finetuning" leave some ambiguity about what defines the reference direction.

feasibility.justification: The hardest step is the "top-k singular directions of the stacked deltas" localization together with reconstructing a projected delta and adding it to the base; these are standard matrix decomposition, parameter-editing, and model-evaluation operations supported by common numerical and deep-learning tooling rather than undefined magic steps. The required models and methods—open-weight instruct models, fine-tuning, parameter differencing, cosine projection, behavioral evaluation, and logistic-regression baselines—exist, while the plan usefully quantifies "6 traits" and "10 independent students per trait" but leaves the exact model, dataset size, prompt count, and training configuration unspecified. The refuting branch is runnable because matched and mismatched directions are compared and the design includes "cross-family teacher," "clean/unrelated data," and surface-feature controls, though teacher construction and trait-strength elicitation would still require protocol choices before execution.
